# Data

<!-- Generated by `mise run catalog:generate` from examples/catalog/: edit the entries, not this file. -->

The data API: pointers that are never `None` and those that can be, subtypes chosen by a Type tag, collections looked
up by name, enum values as strings, and node sockets. Enum properties with dynamic items are in
[Properties](properties.md#dynamic-enum).

<a id="pointers"></a>
## Pointers and `None`

<a id="never-none-pointers"></a>
### Never-None pointers

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/never-none-pointers`

The stubs type a pointer that can never be `None` without `None`, so it is read directly. `camera.dof` is such a
pointer: Blender stores the struct inside the camera, so there is always one. A pointer that can be `None`, such as
`object.pose`, keeps it.

```python
from bpy.types import Camera, CameraDOFSettings, Object, Pose


def example(camera: Camera, ob: Object) -> None:
    assert_type(camera.dof, CameraDOFSettings)
    assert_type(ob.pose, Pose | None)
```

- **What you see:** `camera.dof` is `CameraDOFSettings`; `ob.pose` is `Pose | None`.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs type these pointers as `X | None`: they do not carry which pointers are never `None`. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: These stubs type these pointers as `X | None`: they do not carry which pointers are never `None`.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [`source/blender/makesrna/intern/makesrna.cc`](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/src/branch/main/source/blender/makesrna/intern/makesrna.cc) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/never_none_pointers.py)

<a id="nullable-pointers"></a>
### Pointers `None` until set

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/nullable-pointers`

Some data is created only on demand: an object has no `animation_data` until it is animated or
`animation_data_create()` is called. The stubs type such a pointer as `X | None`, so a read through it is reported until
the code checks it or creates the data.

```python
from bpy.types import AnimData, Object


def example(ob: Object) -> None:
    print(ob.animation_data.action)  # reported: missing-union-attribute
    if ob.animation_data is None:
        assert_type(ob.animation_data_create(), AnimData)
```

- **What you see:** `ob.animation_data_create()` is `AnimData`; ty reports [`missing-union-attribute`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#missing-union-attribute) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/nullable_pointers.py)

<a id="object-data-type"></a>
### `object.data` by type

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/object-data-type`

After a test of `object.type`, in an `if` or a `match`, the checker narrows `object.data` to the data-block that type
holds: a `Mesh` for `"MESH"`. The stubs type `data` as the union of every kind of data-block, and `None` for an empty.

```python
from bpy.types import Camera, Mesh, Object


def example(ob: Object) -> None:
    if ob.type == "MESH":
        assert_type(ob.data, Mesh)
    match ob.type:
        case "CAMERA":
            assert_type(ob.data, Camera)
```

- **What you see:** `ob.data` is `Mesh`; `ob.data` is `Camera`.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs type `object.data` as `ID | None`, with no view of `data` per `type` for the checker to narrow to. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: These stubs have no view of `object.data` per `type`, so it stays the union of all data types.
- **More:** [feature tests: type_narrowing](../../tests/typecheck/features/type_narrowing/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/object_data_type.py)

<a id="pointer-alias"></a>
### Pointers Blender keeps in step

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/pointer-alias`

Blender's C code keeps some pointers in step: in the node editor, `space_data.node_tree` being set means
`space_data.edit_tree` is set too, since Blender sets and clears the two together. The checker applies such a
Pointer alias without reporting it: a poll that checks `node_tree` also covers `edit_tree`. The read of `node_tree`
itself is reported as the narrowing the poll implies; the read of `edit_tree`, which the alias adds, is not.

```python
from bpy.types import NodeTree, Panel


class SIMPLE_PT_node_tree(Panel):
    bl_label = "Node tree"
    bl_space_type = "NODE_EDITOR"
    bl_region_type = "UI"

    @classmethod
    def poll(cls, context):
        return context.space_data.node_tree is not None

    def draw(self, context):
        assert_type(context.space_data.node_tree, NodeTree)  # reported: blender-narrowed-by-poll
        assert_type(context.space_data.edit_tree, NodeTree)
```

- **What you see:** `context.space_data.edit_tree` is `NodeTree`; ty reports [`blender-narrowed-by-poll`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#blender-narrowed-by-poll) (warn) on the line marked *reported*.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs have no Tag views, so `context.space_data` stays `Space | None`, and `Space` has no `node_tree` or `edit_tree`: each read is reported. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: These stubs have no Tag views, so `context.space_data` stays `Space | None`, and `Space` has no `node_tree` or `edit_tree`: each read is reported.
- **More:** [feature tests: pointer_aliases](../../tests/typecheck/features/pointer_aliases/README.md) · [feature tests: implied_narrowings](../../tests/typecheck/features/implied_narrowings/README.md) · [`source/blender/editors/space_node/space_node.cc`](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/src/branch/main/source/blender/editors/space_node/space_node.cc) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/pointer_alias.py)

<a id="collections"></a>
## Collections

<a id="collection-by-name"></a>
### `collection["name"]`

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/collection-by-name`

A collection of Blender data is looked up by name or by index, and both give its element type: an `Object` from
`bpy.data.objects`. Whether the name exists is known only while Blender runs, so a lookup of a missing name is not
reported; `.get()` is the form that can say so.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.types import Object


def example() -> None:
    assert_type(bpy.data.objects["Cube"], Object)
    assert_type(bpy.data.objects[0], Object)
```

- **What you see:** `bpy.data.objects["Cube"]` is `Object`; `bpy.data.objects[0]` is `Object`.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/collection_by_name.py)

<a id="collection-get"></a>
### `.get()`

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/collection-get`

`collection.get(name)` gives the element, or `None` when there is none of that name. The stubs type it as `X | None`,
so a read without a check is reported.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.types import Material


def example() -> None:
    assert_type(bpy.data.materials.get("Rust"), Material | None)
    print(bpy.data.materials.get("Rust").name)  # reported: missing-union-attribute
```

- **What you see:** `bpy.data.materials.get("Rust")` is `Material | None`; ty reports [`missing-union-attribute`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#missing-union-attribute) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs type `.get()` as returning a plain `bpy_struct`, which has no `name`.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/collection_get.py)

<a id="foreach-get"></a>
### `foreach_get`

**Partial**: handled in part by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/foreach-get`

`collection.foreach_get(name, values)` reads one attribute of every element into a flat sequence in one call, much
faster than a loop. The stubs type the call, but the attribute name is a plain string, so a misspelt one is not
reported; the marked line shows the result a check would give.

```python
from bpy.types import Mesh


def example(mesh: Mesh) -> None:
    coords = [0.0] * (len(mesh.vertices) * 3)
    assert_type(mesh.vertices.foreach_get("co", coords), None)
    # not handled yet: the attribute name is not checked
    mesh.vertices.foreach_get("coo", coords)  # would be reported: invalid-argument-type
```

- **What you see:** `mesh.vertices.foreach_get("co", coords)` is `None`.
- **Not yet:** The attribute name is a plain `str`: a misspelt one is not reported.
- **Today:** nothing is reported on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Possible: Check the attribute name against the element type's properties.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/foreach_get.py)

<a id="new-and-remove"></a>
### `new()` and `remove()`

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/new-and-remove`

`new()` creates an element of a collection and returns it; `remove()` deletes one, and takes only an element of that
collection's type. Where the kind of element is an
argument, as for a constraint or a light, the checker types the result as that kind: `constraints.new("COPY_LOCATION")`
is a `CopyLocationConstraint`.

```python
import bpy
from bpy.types import CopyLocationConstraint, Object, SpotLight


def example(ob: Object) -> None:
    constraint = ob.constraints.new("COPY_LOCATION")
    assert_type(constraint, CopyLocationConstraint)
    assert_type(bpy.data.lights.new("Key", "SPOT"), SpotLight)
    ob.constraints.remove(constraint)
    ob.constraints.remove(ob)  # reported: invalid-argument-type
```

- **What you see:** `constraint` is `CopyLocationConstraint`; `bpy.data.lights.new("Key", "SPOT")` is `SpotLight`; ty reports [`invalid-argument-type`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-argument-type) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **With other stubs:** fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender main: The checker narrows by the `rna_enum_*` alias a constructor's kind parameter shares with the Type tag; fake-bpy-module has no such alias, so the result stays the base type. · builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: The checker narrows by the `rna_enum_*` alias a constructor's kind parameter shares with the Type tag; Blender 5.2's builtin stubs have no such alias, so the result stays the base type. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: The checker narrows by the `rna_enum_*` alias a constructor's kind parameter shares with the Type tag; these stubs have no such alias, so the result stays the base type.
- **More:** [feature tests: type_narrowing](../../tests/typecheck/features/type_narrowing/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/new_and_remove.py)

<a id="enums"></a>
## Enum values

<a id="enum-flag-set"></a>
### An enum-flag set

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/enum-flag-set`

An enum-flag property holds a set of identifiers, such as an operator's `bl_options`. The stubs type it as a set of
the `Literal` identifiers, so a misspelt one is reported.

```python
from bpy.types import Operator


class Nudge(Operator):
    bl_idname = "data.nudge"
    bl_label = "Nudge"
    bl_options = {"REGISTER", "UNDOO"}  # reported: invalid-assignment
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/enum_flag_set.py)

<a id="enum-string"></a>
### An enum value as a string

**Handled** by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/enum-string`

An enum property of Blender's takes and gives one of its identifiers as a string. The stubs type it as the `Literal`
of those identifiers, so a misspelt value is reported.

```python
from bpy.types import Object


def example(ob: Object) -> None:
    ob.rotation_mode = "QUATERNION"
    ob.rotation_mode = "XZYY"  # reported: invalid-assignment
    assert_type(ob.display_type, Literal["BOUNDS", "WIRE", "SOLID", "TEXTURED"])
```

- **What you see:** `ob.display_type` is `Literal["BOUNDS", "WIRE", "SOLID", "TEXTURED"]`; ty reports [`invalid-assignment`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#invalid-assignment) (error) on the line marked *reported*.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/enum_string.py)

<a id="nodes"></a>
## Nodes and sockets

<a id="node-by-type"></a>
### `nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")`

**Handled** by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/node-by-type`

`nodes.new` takes the idname of the node to create, as a string. The stubs return a plain `Node`; the checker types
the result as the node the idname names, so its own properties and sockets are known.

```python
from bpy.types import ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled, ShaderNodeTree


def example(tree: ShaderNodeTree) -> None:
    principled = tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")
    assert_type(principled, ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled)
    principled.distribution = "GGX"
```

- **What you see:** `principled` is `ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled`.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs do not give each node class its idname, which the checker reads, so `nodes.new` stays a plain `Node`. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: These stubs do not give each node class its idname, which the checker reads, so `nodes.new` stays a plain `Node`.
- **More:** [feature tests: type_narrowing](../../tests/typecheck/features/type_narrowing/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/node_by_type.py)

<a id="socket-by-name"></a>
### Sockets by name

**Partial**: handled in part by [the stubs](by-safeguard.md#stub-generator) and [the runtime probe](by-safeguard.md#runtime-probe) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/socket-by-name`

A built-in node's sockets are looked up by name, identifier or index, and each has its own socket type: the Principled
BSDF's `"Base Color"` input is a `NodeSocketColor`. Blender's API docs build probes each node for its sockets, and the
stubs carry what it finds. A name the node does not declare gives a plain `NodeSocket` and is not reported; the marked
line shows the result a check would give.

```python
from bpy.types import NodeSocketColor, NodeSocketShader, ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled


def example(principled: ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled) -> None:
    assert_type(principled.inputs["Base Color"], NodeSocketColor)
    assert_type(principled.outputs["BSDF"], NodeSocketShader)
    # not handled yet: a name the node does not declare is not reported
    print(principled.inputs["Base Colour"])  # would be reported: invalid-argument-type
```

- **What you see:** `principled.inputs["Base Color"]` is `NodeSocketColor`; `principled.outputs["BSDF"]` is `NodeSocketShader`.
- **Not yet:** A name the node does not declare gives a plain `NodeSocket`, not an error.
- **Today:** nothing is reported on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Possible: Type the lookup by the node's socket names only, so another name is reported, as fake-bpy-module does for 5.2.
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs do not type a node's sockets by name, so each is a plain `NodeSocket` and the asserts fail. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: These stubs type a node's sockets by an overload of their names, so a name the node does not declare is reported.
- **More:** [feature tests: api_types](../../tests/typecheck/features/api_types/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/socket_by_name.py)

<a id="socket-default-value"></a>
### A socket's `default_value`

**Partial**: handled in part by [the add-on typechecker](by-safeguard.md#typechecker) · checked with Blender main, builtin stubs · `data/socket-default-value`

Every socket type that holds a value has a `default_value`, but the base `NodeSocket` does not. A socket found by a
name that is not a literal is a plain `NodeSocket`; the checker takes it to be one of the socket types with a
`default_value`, accepts the read and reports it as an Assumption. A write there is not accepted yet.

```python
from bpy.types import ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled


def example(principled: ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled, name: str) -> None:
    socket = principled.inputs[name]
    print(socket.default_value)  # reported: blender-assumed-subclass-member
    # not handled yet: a write to a subclass member is an error
    socket.default_value = 0.5
```

- **What you see:** ty reports [`blender-assumed-subclass-member`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#blender-assumed-subclass-member) (warn) on the line marked *reported*.
- **Not yet:** A read of `default_value` on a plain `NodeSocket` is assumed; a write is still an error.
- **Today:** ty reports [`missing-attribute`](https://github.com/taway1450/ruff-blender/blob/blender/crates/ty/docs/rules.md#missing-attribute) (error) on the line marked *not handled yet*.
- **Future:** Planned: Accept a write to a member only a subclass has, as the read is. (tracked: `later/subclass-member-writes`)
- **With other stubs:** builtin stubs, Blender 5.2: Blender 5.2's builtin stubs report the read of `default_value` on `NodeSocket` as missing instead of assuming it. · fake-bpy-module stubs, Blender 5.2: These stubs reject a key that is not a literal name of the node's sockets, so the socket is unknown and neither the read nor the write is reported.
- **More:** [feature tests: assumptions](../../tests/typecheck/features/assumptions/README.md) · [source](../../examples/catalog/data/socket_default_value.py)
